transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well... I guess, honestly, what really made me finally make this appointment and come in today is that I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off. 

I work over at the distribution center, I'm an order filler, so I'm on my feet all day long, just walking up and down the concrete aisles, lifting boxes, constantly moving and checking things off. And usually, you know, when you work a job like that, by the time you clock out, you're just so ready to go home and relax. It's the best part of the day. But lately, I'll get home, and I'll sit on the couch with my husband, or I'll try to watch my regular shows after work—we usually watch a couple of episodes of something before bed just to wind down—and I know, in my head, I know I should feel comfort. I should feel relieved to be home, or even just a little happy to be spending time with him and resting my feet, but... there’s just nothing there. 

It's like this weird blank space where my feelings are supposed to be. He'll make a joke, or something nice will happen on the TV, and I'm just sitting there waiting to feel that little spark of happiness, and it just doesn't come. It's just nothing. And it's been really bothering me, honestly, because I'm not usually like this. I usually love our evenings together, I look forward to them all day while I'm stocking shelves, but now I just sit there and I can't feel any of the good stuff at all.
Has this feeling of not being able to feel happy or enjoy things happened in other parts of your life too, or does it seem to only happen when you're home with your husband watching TV?

Well, gosh, I... I don't really know. I haven't really thought about it happening anywhere else, to be perfectly honest with you, because, well, when I'm at the distribution center, it's not like I'm supposed to be jumping for joy anyway, you know? It's just work. I get there at 6 AM, punch in, grab my scanner, and I'm just completely focused on getting the pallets loaded and making sure the aisle numbers match up. You don't really need to feel happy to scan a barcode or haul a heavy box of detergent. So, I guess I haven't really noticed it there. It's just go, go, go. 

And then on my lunch break, I usually just sit in my car and eat a sandwich—usually just turkey and cheese, nothing special—and maybe scroll on my phone. But I'm just so tired by then that I'm not really looking for happiness, I'm just trying to rest my feet before the second half of the shift. So I really couldn't tell you if it's happening there too, or if it's just that I'm at work and work is work. 

But at home... that's where it really, really stands out to me. Because home is where I *should* be feeling it. Like I was saying, I used to love just pulling into the driveway and seeing the porch light on, knowing I was done for the day. Now I pull in and... nothing. So, I guess I'm just not sure about the rest of my life. I haven't really paid attention to whether it's happening at the grocery store or running errands or whatever. It's mostly just the evenings with my husband that I really notice it, because that's when it feels so incredibly wrong to just be sitting there feeling totally blank when I know I used to feel so warm and cozy.

Have you noticed this lack of enjoyment or inability to feel pleasure in other parts of your life, such as during your workday, while eating, or when doing other routine activities, or does it only seem to happen in the evenings at home?

Well, like I was just saying a second ago, I really don't think I can give you a good answer on that because I just haven't noticed it anywhere else. I mean, work is just work. I don't think anyone feels actual pleasure walking up and down aisle fourteen with a pallet jack, you know? 

And with eating... I mean, I guess maybe I used to enjoy my food a little more? But when you're just sitting in the front seat of a hot car on a strict thirty-minute lunch break, shoving a dry turkey and provolone sandwich in your mouth before you have to go back to lifting fifty-pound boxes, it's not exactly a five-star restaurant experience. I just eat because my stomach is growling and my feet hurt and I need the calories to finish the shift. So I really don't know if I'm missing out on joy there, or if it's just, you know, survival mode. 

And it's the same with routine stuff. Like, I usually go to the grocery store down the street on my way home on Thursdays, and I'm just pushing the cart with a wonky wheel, staring at my list, trying to beat the evening rush so I can just get home. I'm not really checking in with my feelings in the produce aisle. I'm just trying to remember if we need more milk. So I really just couldn't tell you about the rest of the day. It's truly just the evenings at home that I notice it. Because that's the only time I actually stop moving long enough to realize that the warm, cozy feeling I usually get when I finally sit down next to my husband just isn't showing up anymore.
Can you think of any other activities or moments in your day, outside of your evenings at home, where you’ve noticed that things you used to enjoy just don’t feel the same anymore?

Doctor, I feel like I'm a broken record here, but I really, truly don't know how else to explain it to you. Like I've been saying, I just can't think of any other time because it's those evenings that are the whole problem. That's honestly the entire reason I finally picked up the phone and made this appointment. I just feel like the warm part of me completely shut off. 

I mean, think about it—when you're working a shift or running errands, you're not exactly looking for warmth or joy, right? You're just getting through the day. But when I finally sit down with my husband on that couch, or when I turn on one of my shows—like, we've been watching this baking competition lately, which usually I just love, I get so invested in who makes the best cake and the judges and all that—I know in my heart I should be feeling comfort. I know I should be feeling at least a little bit happy to just be there, resting my feet next to him. But there is just absolutely nothing there. 

It's like a switch got flipped and the wiring is just cut. I'm just staring at the TV, or looking at him, and the happiness I'm supposed to feel is just... gone. It's completely absent. So, no, I really can't think of other moments during the day, because those evenings were my main moments of real joy, the thing that got me through all the heavy lifting and the concrete floors, and now they're just blank. It's so frustrating, you know? Because I keep waiting for that warm feeling to come back, every single night, I sit there and wait for it, and every single night it's just the same empty nothing.

Have you noticed any changes in how you feel during other parts of your day, even small things like enjoying your favorite food, noticing something pretty outside, or feeling a sense of accomplishment after finishing a task?

Doctor, I... I just don't know how many different ways I can say this. I feel like we keep going around in circles, and I'm really trying my best to answer you, I really am, but it's just exactly what I've been saying this whole time. I haven't noticed it with food, I haven't noticed it with the weather or the trees outside, I haven't noticed it with finishing a pallet at work. 

Honestly, the entire reason I am sitting in this chair right now, the whole reason I made this appointment and took time off work to come here, is because I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off. It's not about the little things during the day. It's about coming home, taking off my work boots, sitting on the couch with my husband, turning on the TV to watch my shows, and just... nothing. 

I know in my head, I know logically that I should be feeling comfort. I should feel relieved to be off my feet. I should feel a little happy to be sitting next to the man I love after a long day of hauling boxes. But there is just absolutely nothing there. It's like I'm hollowed out. I'm just sitting there, going through the motions, waiting for that cozy, happy feeling to wash over me like it always used to, and it just never comes. So, no, I haven't noticed it with a sandwich or a sunset or whatever. I just notice that the best part of my day, the part where I actually get to be a person and feel good things, is just completely gone.
Outside of not feeling joy in the evenings, do you find yourself feeling down, sad, or hopeless during other parts of your day?

Sad? Hopeless? I mean... no, not really. It's not like I'm walking around crying all day or thinking the world is ending or something. Like, when I'm at the warehouse, I'm just focused on my pick rate and making sure I don't get run over by a forklift. You can't really be hopeless when you have a quota to meet, you know? You just put your head down, pull your pallet, and get the job done. I'm not weeping in the breakroom or feeling sorry for myself while I'm stocking shelves. It's more just... a flatline. 

Like I keep trying to explain, it's not this deep, heavy sadness. I wouldn't use words like "down" or "hopeless" at all, because hopeless sounds like you're just throwing in the towel and giving up. And I'm definitely not giving up. I'm still getting up at five in the morning every single day, I'm still packing my lunch, still clocking in on time, still doing all the grocery shopping and paying the bills. If I was hopeless, I probably wouldn't even be able to drag myself out of bed, right? But I do. I do all of the things I'm supposed to do. 

It's just that... when the day is finally over, and I've done everything right, and I finally get to sit down next to my husband... that's when that blankness hits. It's not sadness. I'm not sitting on the couch crying. It's just... nothing. It's a missing thing, not a sad thing. I really don't know how else to get that across to you, because I feel like we keep trying to find this secret sadness during my day, and it's just not there. I'm just functioning, and then I'm blank. That's really all it is.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in other areas of your life, such as hobbies, time with friends, or other personal moments, even outside of your evenings at home?

Doctor, I... I'm really starting to feel like I'm speaking a different language here. I don't mean to be difficult, I really don't, but I feel like you're asking me the exact same question for the fourth time, just using slightly different words. Hobbies? Friends? Personal moments? I... I don't know how to make this any clearer. 

Look, between the warehouse and the commute, I don't exactly have this huge, bustling social calendar or a bunch of hobbies. I don't knit, I don't play tennis, I don't go out for drinks with the girls. My life is work, and then my life is home. And I'm telling you, the whole reason I made this appointment—the entire reason I am sitting here right now—is because that warm part of me, the part that actually feels good things, just completely shut off. 

I've said this. I sit on the couch with my husband after work, I turn on my shows, and I know—I *know*—I should be feeling comfort. I should feel a little happy to just be there with him. But there is just nothing there. It's not about friends or hobbies or whatever else. It's about the one part of my day that used to actually mean something to me, the one part of my day where I actually got to feel good, and now it's just... it's just a blank space. I don't know what else to tell you. I really don't. I'm just... I'm just empty when I should be happy. That's it. That's the whole thing.

Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in anything else, even things you used to enjoy, like a favorite activity, a hobby, or even small moments like finishing a task or getting praise at work?

Doctor, I... I just don't understand what is happening here. Are you... are you listening to me? I feel like I am losing my mind sitting in this chair right now, because I swear to you, I have just answered this exact same question. I mean, you just asked about finishing a task, you just asked about hobbies, and I... I don't know what else I can possibly say to make this register with you. 

I'm not trying to be difficult, I promise you I'm not. I respect your time, and I know you're the doctor, but I am sitting here practically begging you to hear what I'm saying. I don't care about getting praise at the warehouse. I don't care about hobbies because I don't have time for hobbies. I am a stocker. I pull pallets. I go to work, I sweat, my feet ache, and then I go home. That is my life. 

And I'm telling you again—because it is the only reason I am here, the only reason I took time off to come see you—is that the warm part of me, the part that makes me a human being who feels things, has just completely shut off. It's just gone. When I get home, when I finally get to sit down on the couch next to my husband, when I turn on the TV to watch my shows... that is my time. That is the time when I am supposed to feel good. I know, logically, in my brain, that I should feel comfort. I should feel a little happy to be sitting next to the man I love after a grueling day of work. But there is just absolutely nothing there. 

It's not about a favorite activity. It's not about getting a pat on the back from my manager. It is about the fact that I am sitting in my own living room, with my own husband, doing the one thing that used to bring me peace, and I feel like an empty shell. I don't know how to explain it any better than that. I'm just hollow when I'm supposed to be happy. Please, doctor, please tell me you understand what I'm saying this time, because I really don't think I can explain the couch and the TV and my husband again.

When you're not at home in the evenings, do you notice that you don't feel anything when something good happens, like hearing positive news, seeing something beautiful in nature, or when something special happens unexpectedly?

Are you... are you messing with me right now? Is this some kind of psychological test to see if I'll snap? Because I honestly cannot believe you are asking me this again. 'Seeing something beautiful in nature'? Doctor, I work in a giant, windowless, corrugated metal box. The closest thing I see to nature is a couple of pigeons fighting over a stale french fry in the parking lot when I'm walking to my car at 5:30 in the morning. And 'unexpected special things'? I'm a thirty-six-year-old warehouse stocker. My days are planned down to the fifteen-minute break. There are no unexpected special things happening to me between aisle four and the loading dock! 

I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall. I really, truly do. I don't know how to make you hear me. I don't have these magical moments you keep trying to dig up. I have my routine. I have my work, and I have my home. And honestly, what made me come in—the entire reason I made this appointment and took time off to sit in this chair—is because I feel like the warm part of me just... shut off. Like someone flipped a breaker in my chest and just left it in the dark. 

I sit with my husband after work. I try to watch my shows. That is my 'beautiful nature.' That is my 'special thing.' And I know, I *know* I should feel comfort when I do that. I know I should feel even just a little bit happy to be sitting there with him, resting my feet, just being home. But there’s just nothing there! It is just blank. Empty. Nothing. I am practically screaming this at you. Please, stop asking me about trees and good news and hobbies and just listen to what I am actually telling you about my husband and my couch!

Do you find that you don’t get any pleasure or feel connected when you're with your husband outside of watching TV, like when you're talking, spending quiet time together, or doing something else you used to enjoy?

Oh my god. I... I honestly don't know whether to laugh or just walk out the door right now. Are you reading off a checklist? Is that what's happening? You have a piece of paper in front of you and you just have to ask me about every single possible scenario in my living room? 

Because I feel like I am trapped in some kind of nightmare loop. Yes, doctor. Yes. Talking, quiet time, staring at the ceiling, whatever you want to call it. It's all exactly the same thing! When I say we sit on the couch and watch TV, I don't mean we're just mindless zombies who don't acknowledge each other. That *is* our quiet time. That *is* our talking time. We talk during the commercials, we talk about his day, we talk about how much my feet hurt from the warehouse... that is our time together. That's my whole marriage right there in those few hours.

And honestly, like I have been trying to drill into your head for the last twenty minutes, what made me come in here today is that I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off. It doesn't matter if the TV is on or off. It doesn't matter if he's talking to me or if we're just sitting there in dead silence. I sit with my husband, or I try to watch my shows after work, and I know—I know in my head—that I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even a little happy just to be near him, because he's a good man and he's trying his best to be supportive. But there’s just nothing there. 

It's just a void. So please, I am begging you, just write it down on your notepad. Write down 'she feels absolutely nothing.' Underline it. Circle it. Highlight it. Because I cannot keep explaining my evenings to you. I'm telling you my feelings are just gone, and you keep asking me if they're gone while we talk, or while we sit, or while we watch TV. It's all of it! It's just nothing! Please, for the love of god, tell me we can talk about something else now. Please.

So you feel this blankness mainly when you're with your husband in the evenings—can you tell me if you ever feel this same lack of feeling at other times, even when you're alone or doing something by yourself?

I... I actually think I might scream. I really do. Are you listening to the words coming out of my mouth, or are you just waiting for your turn to speak so you can ask me the exact same question with one word changed? 'When you're alone.' Doctor, listen to me. Please. Look at me and listen. 

I am going to say this one last time, and I want you to write it down word for word so we can finally move on. The entire reason I am sitting in this office today—honestly, what made me come in and spend my hard-earned money on this appointment—is because I feel like the warm part of me has just completely shut off. It does not matter if my husband is sitting right next to me. It does not matter if he is in the kitchen and I am completely by myself. The situation does not change the fact that the feeling is gone! 

I sit there, by myself or with him, and I try to watch my shows after work. That is my routine. And I know—I know logically, in my brain—that I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even just a little happy to finally be off my aching feet, just to be resting, whether I'm alone or not. But there is just nothing there. 

It’s like you think if I just move to a different room, or if I’m by myself instead of with him, suddenly a magic switch is going to flip and I’m going to feel joy again. That’s not how this works! It’s a constant, heavy, empty blankness. It’s not a 'husband' problem, it’s not a 'TV' problem, it’s a *me* problem. My emotions are just gone. The warm, human part of me is running on dead batteries. So no, being alone doesn't change it. Being with him doesn't change it. It is all the time, every single time I try to just relax and feel something good. Do you finally understand what I am telling you?
Do you feel this blankness only in the evenings after work, or do you also notice it at other times when you're not working, like in the mornings or on your days off?

Are you... are you getting paid by the question? Is there a hidden camera in here? Because I genuinely cannot comprehend how we are still doing this. Mornings. Evenings. Days off. Tuesdays. Sundays. Leap years! Doctor, it does not matter what time the clock says! 

Let me walk you through a Sunday, since apparently you need every single hour of my week accounted for before you'll believe me. I wake up. I don't have to go to the warehouse. I make coffee. I sit on the exact same couch. And honestly, like I have been saying since I first walked through that door—what made me come in here is that I feel like the warm part of me just shut off. Completely. It doesn't magically turn back on just because it's a weekend! 

I sit there with my husband on my day off, or I try to watch my morning shows instead of my after-work shows, and I know... I *know* I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even just a little happy that I don't have to be on my feet all day, that I get to just rest and be a normal person. But there’s just nothing there! It is the exact same nothing I feel at 7 PM on a Wednesday! 

It’s like you’re trying to find some kind of loophole in my brain. 'Oh, maybe she feels joy at 10 AM on a Saturday!' No! I don't! The battery is dead. The breaker is flipped. Morning, noon, and night. So please, can we stop going through my schedule hour by hour? The blankness is always there. Always.
Do you feel this same lack of pleasure or emotional flatness even when you're interacting with people outside of your husband, like friends or coworkers?

I... I honestly don't even know what to say anymore. I really don't. Are you just going down a list of every single person I could possibly ever interact with in my entire life? Friends? Coworkers? Who’s next, the mailman? The guy who bags my groceries? My third-grade teacher? 

Because I can save us both a whole lot of time right now. Yes! Yes, it is the exact same with them! I am at the warehouse all day, pulling orders, stocking shelves, working alongside the exact same people I’ve known for years. We eat lunch together. We complain about our feet together. And it is the exact... same... blankness. I’m standing there, and they're joking around or talking about their kids, and I just feel completely hollow. 

Like I have been telling you over and over and over again—honestly, what made me come in here today, the whole reason I made this appointment in the first place, is because I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off! It’s gone! I sit with my husband, or I try to watch my shows after work, or I sit in the breakroom with my coworkers, and I know I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even a little happy to be around people I like, or happy to just be sitting down for five minutes! But there’s just nothing there. 

It doesn’t matter if it’s my husband, my friends, or a guy driving a forklift. The warmth is gone. It doesn't matter who is standing in front of me. So please, I am begging you, do not ask me if I feel this way with my cousins, or my neighbors, or the people on the bus. Just write down that the feeling is gone for everyone, everywhere, all the time. Can we please, please just move on to something else?

Can you tell me if you feel this same blankness or lack of emotion even in moments when you're completely alone and not engaged in your usual routines, like when you're getting ready in the morning or just sitting quietly by yourself?

I... I am actually speechless. I am sitting here, looking at you, and I am completely speechless. Did you just ask me about getting ready in the morning? After I literally just told you to write down that it is everyone, everywhere, all the time? Are you messing with me? Is this some kind of psychological test to see how long it takes for a person to lose their mind in a doctor's office? Because if it is, you are winning! 

But fine. Okay. Let us talk about getting ready in the morning! Let us talk about me standing in front of my bathroom mirror at 5:30 AM, staring at the wall, brushing my teeth, completely by myself. Not in my usual routine, just sitting quietly on the edge of the tub. You want to know what I feel? Nothing! Like I keep telling you! 

Honestly, and I am going to say this one more time, what made me come in here is that I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off. It is gone! I sit with my husband, or I try to watch my shows after work, or I sit on the edge of my bathtub by myself in the dead quiet of the morning, and I know I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even a little happy to just have a peaceful moment before I have to go bust my back at the warehouse. But there is just nothing there! 

It is a void! It is blank! Whether I am brushing my hair, tying my shoes, sitting quietly, or staring at the ceiling, it does not matter! I do not know how many different ways I can explain this to you. The warm part is off. Nothing is there. Can we please, for the love of everything, talk about something else now?
So you're saying this emotional blankness is constant, not tied to any specific time, place, or person—it's just always there, all the time?

Yes! Yes, exactly! That is exactly what I have been trying to tell you for I don't even know how long now! It is constant. It never stops. It never changes. 

I mean, I don't know how else to say it. Honestly, what made me come in here, what finally made me pick up the phone and make this appointment after putting it off for weeks, is that I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off. Like somebody just reached in and flipped a switch, and now everything is just... cold. Flat. 

I sit with my husband on the couch, or I try to watch my shows after work—you know, the ones I used to actually look forward to all day while I was hauling boxes around the warehouse—and I know I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even a little happy just to be home, just to be with him, just to have my feet up. I remember what that used to feel like. But now? There’s just nothing there. It's just empty. And it is like that all the time. Always. So yes, you finally got it. It is constant.
Can you tell me if you've completely lost the ability to feel pleasure or interest in anything at all, even things you used to enjoy or in moments of quiet by yourself?

I... I am seriously wondering if I am speaking a different language right now. I really am. Are you... are you just reading the same question off your clipboard but phrasing it slightly differently every time? Because I swear, I have just answered this. I just said it! I just said it was constant! 

But okay. Okay, fine. I will say it again, with as many words as I possibly can, just so we are absolutely, one hundred percent clear. Yes! I have completely lost the ability to feel pleasure or interest in anything! Anything! Even the things I used to enjoy! Even in the quiet moments! 

I mean, honestly, what made me come in here—and I know I’ve said this already, but I am going to say it again because apparently it’s not sinking in—what made me finally make this appointment is that I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off. It is gone. It is dead. I sit with my husband on the couch in the evening, or I try to watch my shows after work—my favorite shows, the ones I used to actually care about, the ones I used to talk about with the girls in the breakroom—and I know I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even a little happy. I should feel something! But there’s just nothing there! 

It is like I am a ghost in my own life. I used to love coming home, kicking my shoes off, and just sinking into the couch with him. I used to love that! And now I just sit there, staring at the TV, staring at the wall, staring at whatever, and I am just... empty. So yes. Yes, to answer your question for the fourth time, I have lost the ability to feel pleasure in anything. Can we please, please, please move on to the next question on your clipboard now?
Can you tell me if you've completely lost the ability to feel pleasure or interest in anything at all, even things you used to enjoy or in moments of quiet by yourself?

I... I honestly don't know what's happening right now. Are you... are you having a stroke? Is this a hidden camera show? I am literally staring at you, and you just asked me the exact same question word-for-word. The exact same question! I just answered this! I just spent like five minutes talking about this!

But you know what? Fine. We can do this all day. I have nowhere else to be. I took the whole afternoon off from the warehouse for this, so let's just keep going in circles! 

Yes, doctor. Yes. I have completely lost the ability to feel pleasure or interest in anything at all. Like I said—and I will say it again, maybe you should write it down this time—what made me finally come in here, what made me realize something was seriously wrong, is that I feel like the warm part of me just completely shut off. It's like someone unplugged me from the wall. 

I sit with my husband on the couch, or I try to watch my shows after a long shift of throwing boxes around, and I know I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even a little happy. I mean, my husband is a good man, he tries to make me laugh, he brings me tea, and I just sit there like a lump of clay. I know I should feel something! But there’s just nothing there. No pleasure, no interest, no happiness, no comfort. Nothing. 

So, yes. For the fifth time. Yes. Do you want me to spell it out? Or are you going to ask me again in two minutes? Because if you ask me this one more time, I might actually lose my mind.
Can you confirm that you've completely lost the ability to feel pleasure or interest in anything at all, even things you used to enjoy or during quiet moments by yourself?

Are you... are you serious right now? I am actually looking around for a hidden camera. I really am. You just asked me that. You just asked me that exact same question. I mean, word for word, the exact same thing. Are you messing with me? Is this some kind of psychological test to see how long it takes for a person to snap? Because if it is, you're getting really close. 

I don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you. I really don't. But I guess I'll just keep talking since that's what I'm paying for, right? I'm paying to sit here and repeat myself to a doctor who apparently isn't listening to a single word I say. 

Look, honestly, what made me come in here—and I feel like a broken record, I really do—what made me come in is I feel like the warm part of me just... shut off. It's completely gone. Like someone flipped a switch in my brain or my heart or wherever it is that you feel things, and now it's just dark in there. 

I sit with my husband, right? He's sitting there on the couch, maybe he's talking about his day, maybe he's trying to get me to laugh. Or I try to watch my shows after work. I stand on my feet all day at the warehouse, pulling orders, stocking shelves, dealing with the noise and the dust, and all I used to want was to come home and watch my shows. And I sit there now, and I know I should feel comfort. I know I should feel even a little happy just to be sitting down, just to be with him, just to have a quiet moment to myself. But there’s just nothing there. 

It's not sadness. It's not anger. It's just... nothing. A big, empty hole where all the good stuff used to be. So yes. Yes, doctor. For the millionth time, yes, I have lost the ability to feel pleasure or interest in anything. Now, please, I am begging you, can we talk about something else? Anything else?

He'll make a joke, or something nice will happen on the TV, and I'm just sitting there waiting to feel that little spark of happiness, and it just doesn't come. It's just nothing.
